title: Normalized ordinary and derived signed Tate reduction
statement: For a prime l, a finite extension E of Q_l, and a scheme X on which l is invertible in every residue field, the structure TateReduction l E X [def-sp-twisted-pullback-reduction-data] is inhabited. This consists only of the first Tate-line scalar quotient comparison and its quotient-unit formula, all signed powers and their normalization, ordinary reduction normalized on scalar tensor generators, K-flatness of the degree-zero signed lines, and the specified composite computing their finite derived reductions. Coefficient fields, completed coefficient sheaves, strict systems and the fixed derived presentations are as in [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension], [def-weil-completed-integral-coefficients], [def-coefficient-twists-detailed], [def-coef-derived-system-calculus-data].

proof.text: Reduce the compatible first root system through its defining scalar quotient map. The map sends the class of 1 tensor x to the class of 1 tensor x, so its generator equation is the prescribed first_unit formula. Local rank-one trivializations show it is an isomorphism.

proof.text: Extend this comparison by signedLineComparison. At zero use the coefficient unitor, at positive powers use balanced reassociation, and at negative powers send phi tensor c to the functional (x tensor t ↦ residue(phi(x))*c*t). These formulas establish the signed normalization. The universal tensor-extension comparison identifies the ordinary scalar extension with its recorded model on every scalar tensor generator.

proof.text: Each signed line is locally free of rank one, hence flat and K-flat in degree zero. Define each level comparison by exactly the composite prescribed in level_formula: single localization, reduction evaluation, K-flat reduction counit, and the ordinary scalar comparison. Every factor is an isomorphism, and the formula is definitional.
